title: Apply Graphic Image
content: ### Objective Place graphic images on Patterns. Use this function to express Garment details such as placed prints, embroideries, or logos. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Graphics ▶ Graphic (2D Pattern) / Graphic (3D Pattern) 3D or 2D Toolbar ▶ Graphic.png Graphic (2D Pattern) / Graphic (3D Pattern) ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Graphics ▶ Graphic (2D Pattern) or Graphic (3D Pattern) 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ Graphic.png Graphic (2D Pattern) or Graphic (3D Pattern) 2. The file browser appears. → Select a graphic image file and load. 3. Click on a Pattern where the graphic image should be placed. → The Add Graphic window appears. 4. Enter the desired values for the graphic dimensions and position: Width | Set the width of the graphic image. ---|--- Height | Set the height of the graphic image. ![Captura de pantalla \(111\).png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438341118361) | Link or unlink the aspect ratio of the graphic image. Position | Outline | Set the distance from the left, right, top, or bottom of the graphic outline to the pattern outline. This menu only appears when placing the graphic in the 2D window (Ver. 2.5.0). Center | Set the distance from the center of the graphic to the left, right, top, or bottom of the pattern outline. This menu only appears when placing the graphic in the 2D window (Ver. 2.5.0). 5. Click OK to place the graphic image. ※ Note: * Add graphics directly by right-clicking on a thumbnail of an image file in the Library window, then select Add as Graphic from the pop-up menu (ver2.4.0). * When importing an AI file with multiple artboards as a graphic, the AI/PDF window appears where artboards can be reviewed and the desired artboard can be selected (Ver. 4.0.0). * PBR maps for Displacement, Opacity, Roughness, and Metalness channel can be automatically generated for the applied graphic image using PBR Map Generator (ver. 2024.1)
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to guide users in placing graphic images on garment patterns, allowing them to effectively display details such as prints, embroideries, and logos in both 2D and 3D formats.

title: Add Point to Intersection
content: Objective Add Segment Points to where segments intersect. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern 2. Select the segment that is crossed. → The selected segment is highlighted in yellow. 3. Right click on the selected segment. → A pop-up menu appears. 4. Select the Add Point to Intersection option. → A Segment Point is added to where the segment intersects. ※Note: * The point is only added to the selected segment. * To add points to both intersecting segments, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard and select both segment before right-clicking and selecting Add Point to Intersection option.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for adding segment points at intersection locations within a 2D pattern editing tool.

title: Show/Hide Button
content: ### Objective Show or hide all buttons and buttonholes. ### Location 3D Garment Window ▶ 3D Garment Display (Mouse-over) ▶ Show Button ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Garment Window ▶ 3D Garment Display (Mouse-over) ▶ Show Button → All buttons and buttonholes are now being hidden. 2. Follow the indicated guideline once again. → All hidden buttons and buttonholes are now being displayed.
content_description: This web page allows users to easily toggle the visibility of buttons and buttonholes in the 3D Garment Display for enhanced garment visualization.

title: Delete
content: ### Objective Delete points, lines, Internal Shapes, and Patterns. ### Location #### Delete Point/Line Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern #### Delete Pattern Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Transform Pattern or Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern or Edit Pattern ### Operation #### Delete Point/Line 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern 2. Right click on the item to be deleted and select Delete on the pop-up menu. → The selected item is deleted. #### Delete Pattern 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Transform Pattern or Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern or Edit Pattern 2. Right click on the item to be deleted and select Delete on the pop-up menu. → The selected item is deleted.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for deleting points, lines, internal shapes, and patterns in a 2D design interface.

title: Create Button
content: ### Objective Create buttons and place them as desired. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Button ### Operation #### Create Button 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Button 2. Click on a desired point on the 3D Garment or 2D Pattern. → A button is now being created at the designated location. #### Input Measurement for Button Position 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Button 2. Right-click on the 2D Pattern where buttons would be placed. → Moving Distance window appears. 3. Input desired measurements for accurate placement. → Placement preview depending on the input value displays along the mouse in the 2D window. 4. Click OK to place. → The buttons are now being created.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for creating and accurately placing buttons on 3D garments and 2D patterns using the Button 3D Toolbar.

title: MODULAR MODE: Create Custom Blocks
content: ### Objective Create a Block of a desired Garment and apply it to your design. ### Location Open Modular Template Modular Mode ▶ Block Editor ▶ Modular Template Presets Load and Place Patterns Modular Mode ▶ Block Editor Sew Patterns to Block Boxes Modular Mode ▶ Block Editor ### Operation Open Modular Template 1\. Follow the indicated guideline below: Modular Mode ▶ Block Editor ▶ Modular Template Presets → Modular Template Presets window appears. ![Captura](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438578872601) ![Captura](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438590200217) 2\. Select a desired Garment category and Modular Template type, click OK. → The selected Modular Template appears in the 2D window. ![Captura](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438579247385) Load and Place Patterns 1\. With a Modular Template opened, follow the indicated guideline below: Modular Mode ▶ Block Editor 2\. Add desired Garment files to place into the Block Boxes. 3\. From the added Garment files, click and drag the Patterns to the matching Block Boxes. → The Patterns are linked into the Block Boxes and Block Boxes turn into dark grey. 4\. Sew Patterns to Block Boxes, then Simulate. Sew Patterns to Block Boxes 1\. Follow the indicated guideline below: Modular Mode ▶ Block Editor 2\. Click on Segment Sewing or Free Sewing tool. 3.Sew Patterns and Block Boxes. → Sewn parts of the Block Boxes turn into darker grey. ※ Note: * Block Boxes are sewn together by default. * Patterns that are sewn alone (i.e. hems, sleeves or armholes of a sleeveless style) do not need to be sewn to Block Boxes. * Difference in length between the actual Patterns and the Block Boxes has no effect on the Simulation. * Rest of the principle is the same as the Simulation Mode. * To show Sewing Lines between Block Boxes and Patterns, activate the Show Modular Sewing/Show Pattern Sewing tool. This tool is activated by default in the Modular Mode. Click it again to either hide or show all Sewing Lines.
content_description: "Learn how to create and apply a desired garment block to your design using the Modular Template and Block Editor in Modular Mode."

title: Guide for Installing Network Offline Version in the Same Network Environment
content: ### Guide for Installing Network Offline Version in the Same Network Environment ### Objective Install Network version in the same Network Environment when Server (PC connected to the red HASP Key) is unable to recognize Client (PC to run the software). ### 1.) Check-up on HASP Driver Installation on Server PC Operation 1\. Access to the Web Browser: [http://localhost:1947](http://localhost:1947/_int_/ACC_help_index.html) Check Sentinel HASP Driver is installed and operating on Server as shown in the image below. ![000.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438682562457) 2\. If the web page does not appear, reinstall Sentinel HASP Driver. [**HASP Driver Install Guide**](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358254274585) ### ### 2.) Additional Set-up ACC Page on Client PC ### Operation 1\. Set up ACC page on PC you want to run the software. 2\. ACC Page : [http://localhost:1947](http://localhost:1947/_int_/ACC_help_index.html) 3\. Click on Configuration (the red box in the image below). ![2323.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438693330457) 4\. Click Access to Remote License Managers. ![4545.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438682830361) 5\. Check on 'Aggressive Search for Remote Licenses' (image below) and type the Server PC IP in "Specify Search Parameters" then click Submit. ※ Note: How to check your IP: Windows Search ▶ Search 'Cmd.exe' ▶ Type 'ipconfig' [http://www.ghacks.net/2011/05/17/network-troubleshooting-basics-the-ipconfig-command/](https://www.ghacks.net/2011/05/17/network-troubleshooting-basics-the-ipconfig-command/) ![4444.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438683135257) 6\. Wait for 10 seconds and its completed when HASP key page shows up (image below). If the page does not show up, the Server and Client may possibly be connected to different network environment. In that case, follow the link below, follow the guideline and try again. [Guideline for Installing Network Version on the Internet Environment](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358458287641) ![6666.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438683220121)
content_description: This webpage serves as a comprehensive guide for installing the Network Offline Version of the software in the same network environment, ensuring seamless recognition between the Server and Client PCs.

Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Color → The Color Palette window appears. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Color → The Color Palette window appears. 2. Click on **Save as Palette** icon on the left side of the palette window. → The selected color is now being saved as *.aco file format.

Object Browser ▶ Select an item in the button tab. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Button Tab ▶ Copy → A new button item with the same properties of the selected item is now being created.

title: Elastic
content: ### Objective Insert elastic to the outer/internal lines of a Pattern to express shirring details. ### Location Pattern Property Editor ▶ Select a Line ▶ Elastic ### Operation 1. Select a outer or internal line with Transform Pattern or Edit Pattern tool. 2. Follow the indicated guideline: Pattern Property Editor ▶ Select a Line ▶ Elastic 3. Click the checkbox and set it On. 4. Adjust the intensity and ratio of the elastic. ※ Note: #### Elastic Properties Elastic | Decides whether to insert an elastic or not. Even though adjusting the value of intensity and ratio is not going to be applied, if this is not being checked. ---|--- Strength | Increase or decrease the elastic intensity value. Even if elastic that has the same ratio, may be affected differently depending on their intensity. Ratio | Shows the elastic ratio when the selected segment is set at 100%. Various garment can be expressed by adjusting the elastic ratio. The elastic ratio can be set up to 200% of the maximum segment. Length | Adjusts the elastic when the length value is entered. If multiple segments are selected, the entered value will be applied to each segment. Entire Length | If multiple segments are selected, the entered value will be applied as the total length of the combined segments.
content_description: This web page guides users on how to apply elastic shirring details to patterns by utilizing the Pattern Property Editor.

title: Show Camera
content: ### Objective Display FBX imported Cameras on the 3D window. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Show Camera ### Operation 1\. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Display ▶Environment ▶ Show Camera → The Camera is now being displayed in the 3D window.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to guide users on how to display FBX imported cameras in the 3D window through the main menu options.

title: Arrange Pattern with Arrangement Points/Flip Wrap Direction
content: ### ### ### ### Objective Arrangement Points are created based on the Bounding Volume surrounding the Avatar, and are arranged on the Avatar according to the Bounding Volume's curves. ※ Note: Precise arrangement is available by using Gizmo or Property Editor even after arranging with Arrangement Points. ### Location Avatar Display ▶ Show Arrangement Points ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline: Avatar Display ▶ Show Arrangement Points → The Arrangement Points appear around the Avatar. 2. Select a Pattern and hover the mouse over an Arrangement Point. → A preview of the Pattern placement is being displayed (ver2.4.0). 3. Select a desired Arrangement Point. → The center of the Pattern is now being placed according to the selected Arrangement Point. → Symmetric Arrangement occurs as long as the Patterns and Arrangement Points have symmetry applied (ver3.0.0). ※ Note: #### Flip Wrap Direction Patterns that the length are longer than the Bounding Volume, such as cuffs, get arranged spiral. Right-click on patterns in the 3D window ▶ Click Flip Wrap Direction to flip its direction.
content_description: This web page provides a detailed guide on how to arrange patterns around an Avatar using Arrangement Points and offers tools for precise placement and adjustments.

title: Roll Up (ver. 12.2)
content: ## Feature Overview Makes it easier to fold the ends of garments, such as sleeve openings, pants openings, etc. ### Steps 1\. Select an outline of the 2D pattern with the Edit Pattern tool. \- Roll Up does not work on outlines contains a sewing relationship to another pattern. \- Roll Up might not work on some segment lines as this feature is optimized for sleeve openings and pants openings that creates a tube. 2\. Follow the indicated guideline below. \- In 2D Window select a segment line, Right Mouse Button click ▶ Roll Up 3\. The Roll Up dialog box appears. Enter the desired input. Number of Roll Up | Set the number of Roll up to 3 times. ---|--- Distance | Enter a minimum of 10mm and a maximum of 200mm as the distance of each roll up Reset | While the dialog box is running, reset the applied Roll Up. Returning the garment to its original state. Apply | Apply Roll Up based on the input values entered. Close | Close the Roll Up dialog box. \- Once you enter the Number of Roll Up and Distance, a green circle will be displayed at the end position of the final garment in the 3D Window as a preview. \- Roll Up does not apply symmetrically or to instance modifications. ### End Result Select Close at the bottom of the dialog to exit Roll Up. \- If the Particle Distance of the pattern being rolled up is over 10mm, it will be automatically adjusted to 10 for stable simulation.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for using the Roll Up feature to efficiently fold garment openings, such as sleeves and pant hems, in a 2D pattern design.

title: Merge Symmetric Patterns
content: ### Objective Merge symmetric Patterns into a single Pattern. ### Location Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern Outline) ▶ Merge ### Operation 1. Navigate to 2D toolbar and select Edit Pattern tool. 2. Right click on the Pattern outline of either symmetric Pattern and follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern Outline) ▶ Merge → The symmetric Patterns are merged into a single Pattern as their Linked Editing function is removed. ※ Note: When there is any point on the selected segment to merge Patterns, the Patterns cannot be merged.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for merging symmetric Patterns into a single Pattern using the Right Click Pop-Up Menu in the 2D toolbar.

title: Project with Meta Data (*.ZPrj)/ Garment with Meta Data (*.zpac)
content: ### Objective When saving Project files, an accompanying XML file with Garment, trim, and texture information will be provided. Turntable images will also be generated with the Project file (versions after 3.1.38) XML File Contents 1\. Product version 2\. Garment version 3\. Garment polygon, triangle, vertex count: this includes the pattern, trims, textures; all information related to the Garment. 3-1. Pattern polygon, triangle, vertex count 3-2. Trim Object polygon, triangle, vertex count: Trim are Object files imported via File » Import » Import as Trim. 3-3. Button polygon, triangle, and vertex count 3-4. Print Texture polygon, triangle, vertex count: Print Texture are textures imported as Graphic. 3-5. Texture Count: the number of textures applied to Fabric. 3-6. Material Count: the number of items used or applied to Fabric. 4\. Avatar total polygon, triangle, and vertex count 5\. Turntable image names --- ### Location Save as Project: Main Menu Save As Project with Metadata/ Garment with Meta Data ### Operation Save as Project 1. Navigate to the menu listed in Location. Save File window will appear. 2. Navigate to the desired file location. 3. Enter a file name in File Name, then click the Save button. 4. The Save Metadata dialogue will appear. File | Save Folder | Saves the Project file along with the metadata and turntable images within a folder. ---|---|--- Save .zip File | Saves the Project file along with the metadata and turntable images as a ZIP file. Image | Image Count | Select the number of images for the Turntable. *** Don't Show Again Check Box** Checking this box will hide the dialog, but will remember the last entered settings when saving the metadata. To view the dialog again, go to Main Menu » User Settings » Others » Metadata, then set the Don't Show Again Save Metadata option to Off.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on saving Project files with accompanying XML metadata and turntable images, detailing the necessary steps and file contents for effective project management.

title: Move with Arrow Keys (3D)
content: ### Objective Select Patterns in the 3D window, then use the arrow keys on the keyboard to move them in specific increments. ### Location #### Move Patterns with Arrow Keys Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Select/Move 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move #### Set Specific Movement Increment Main Menu ▶ Preferences ▶ Grid Properties ▶ Property Editor ▶ 3D Arrow Key Movement Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D Window) ▶ Grid Properties ▶ Property Editor ▶ 3D Arrow Key Movement ### Operation #### Move Patterns with Arrow Keys 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Select/Move 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move 2. Select Patterns or trims in the 3D window. → Selected Patterns or trims are highlighted in yellow. 3. Use the arrow keys on the keyboard to move the selected Pattern or trim. Arrow Keys | Description ---|--- ▲ | Move selected Patterns or trims along or towards the positive y-axis. The Garment moves upwards. ▼ | Move selected Patterns or trims along or towards the negative y-axis. The Garment moves downwards. ◀ | Move selected Patterns or trims along or towards the negative x-axis. The Garment moves to the left. ▶ | Move selected Patterns or trims along or towards the positive x-axis. The Garment moves to the right. ▲+ Ctrl | Move selected Patterns or trims along or towards the negative z-axis. The Garment moves away from you. ▼+ Ctrl | Move selected Patterns or trims along or towards the positive z-axis. The Garment moves towards you. #### Set Specific Movement Increment 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Preferences ▶ Grid Properties ▶ Property Editor ▶ 3D Arrow Key Movement Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D Window) ▶ Grid Properties ▶ Property Editor ▶ 3D Arrow Key Movement 2. Enter the desired distance moved with each arrow key input.
content_description: This webpage provides instructions for selecting and moving patterns in a 3D window using arrow keys, along with guidance on setting specific movement increments for precise adjustments.

title: Create Buttonholes along Pattern Outline (Ver. 5.1)
content: ### Objective Create buttonholess along a Pattern Outline in a constant interval and distance. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Buttonhole 3D Toolbar ▶ Buttonhole ### Operation **Create** 1. Follow the indicated path below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Buttonhole 3D Toolbar ▶ Buttonhole 2. Right click on a Pattern Outline. → The Create Buttons/Buttonholes along Pattern Outline window appears. ※Note: To select multiple lines, press down the Shift key and click the lines to be selected. 3. Configure below options as needed: Start Position | Distance | Set the distance between the buttonholes and the selected line. ---|---|--- Interval | Set the distance between the buttonholes and the Pattern Outline. Reverse | The direction of which buttonholes are created is reversed to the Start Point. Replicate | Interval | Adjust the distance between the buttonholes. Number of Button/Buttonholes | Adjust the number of buttonholes to be created. 4. Click OK. → Buttonholes are created as a group. **Select** 1. Follow the indicated path below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button 2. Click on a buttonhole or a Pattern Outline where buttonholes are created. → All buttonholes in a group are selected. ※Note: Click again while the group of buttonholes are selected to select a single buttonhole. 3. Change selected buttonholes' properties or style or use right-click pop-up menu. → Any changes made are applied to all buttonholes in the same group. → Group information cannot be copied or duplicated. → A pop-up menu is available when right-clicking above the group line with the buttonhole tool. ※Note: Grouped buttonholes cannot be moved. **Unlink** 1. Follow the indicated path below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button 2. Right click on the buttonholes or the Pattern Outline and select Unlink Buttons/Buttonholes. → The link between the buttonholes are removed.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for creating, selecting, and unlinking buttonholes along a pattern outline in a 3D design environment.

title: Internal Ellipse
content: ### Objective Create internal ellipses or circles within Patterns. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ Internal Ellipse 2D Toolbar ▶ Internal Ellipse ### Operation #### Create Internal Ellipse 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ Internal Ellipse 2D Toolbar ▶ Internal Ellipse 2. Click and drag within a Pattern to freehand an ellipse. Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to create a circle. 3. Release the mouse to complete the Internal Ellipse or the Internal Circle. ※ Note: While creating the Internal Shape, press down the Ctrl key on the keyboard to create it by the center point (ver.5.1.0). While creating the Internal Shape, press down the Shift + Ctrl keys to create a full circle by its center point (ver.5.1.0). #### Create Internal Ellipse with Entered Values 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ Internal Ellipse 2D Toolbar ▶ Internal Ellipse 2. Click once within a Pattern. → The Create Ellipse window appears. 3. Enter the desired values. Diameter | Set the diameter of the Internal Circle. ---|--- Radius | Set the radius of the Internal Circle (ver3.2.0). Link to maintain the width and height ratio. Circumference | Set the circumference of the Internal Circle (ver3.2.0). Position | To Outline | Set the position of the left, right, top, and bottom of the Internal Circles from the Pattern outline (ver2.5.0). To Center | Set the position of the center of the Internal Circle from the left, right, top, and bottom of the Pattern outline (ver2.5.0). ※ Note: Internal Shape Tool Group
content_description: This webpage provides instructions for creating internal ellipses or circles within 2D Patterns using the designated tools and settings.

title: Updating Network Software License
content: To update existing Software License Key due to renewing license or adding copies, please follow the instruction below. 1\. Generate C2V file with**the RUS executable file** , located at the bottom of this post, and submit your C2V file through [**this page**](https://marvelousdesigner.com/teamconsole/keyupdate/1) (Logging in with your Company ID is required). If you experience any difficulties, please contact us via support@marvelousdesigner.com ![mceclip0.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438742023449) 2\. The Marvelous Designer Team will send back a V2C file for your license update. 3\. Update the received V2C file by directing the RUS to the folder location of your V2C file at the bottom of the "Apply License File" tab and then clicking "Apply Update". ![2.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438742207641) ### Double checking an updated License Key If the License Key Update process is successfully completed, you will be able to double check by following the steps below. 1\. Open a web browser and access to [http://localhost:1947](http://localhost:1947/_int_/ACC_help_index.html) 2\. Make sure all the information is in this part. 3\. Click Features once you see the key info. ![6.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438742446745) 4\. Make sure the number in the red box has been changed correctly. ![7.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438742615065)
content_description: This webpage provides step-by-step instructions for updating your Software License Key for Marvelous Designer, including generating a C2V file, submitting it for processing, and verifying the successful update.

title: Seamline Topstitch (ver MD10)
content: ### Objective Create a Seamline Topstitch. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Topstitch ▶ Seamline Topstitch 2D Toolbar ▶ Seamline Topstitch ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline above. → All sewing lines on the Pattern are displayed. 2. Click on a point where a Topstitch begins. 3. Move mouse to the direction where the Topstitch is going to be created. 4. Click on another point where the Topstitch ends. → The Topstitch is now being created with being highlighted. **※ Note:** * Click and drag in the 2D window to encompass all segments where Topstitches to be applied. Topstitches appear on all selected segments. * Use lasso selection to select Pattern Outlines and Internal Lines where Topstitches should be created on. * OBJ Topstitches temporarily disappear when the Simulation is activated, but they appear again when the Simulation is deactivated. * Right click when creating the Topstitch to enter specific length.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide on how to create a Seamline Topstitch using the 2D Toolbar within the sewing pattern interface.

title: TOPSTITCH STYLE PROPERTIES: Number of Topstitch Line Setting
content: ### Objective Set how many lines of Topstitches there are for a single style. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ Property Editor ▶ Number of Lines ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ Property Editor ▶ Number of Lines 2. Enter the number of lines as desired. → The Number of Lines is now being adjusted and applied. #### ※ Note : #### Distance of Number of Lines It is possible to adjust the distance between the lines.
content_description: This webpage provides guidance on setting and adjusting the number of topstitch lines for a specific style using the Property Editor in the Object Browser.

title: Segment Sewing (2D)
content: ### Objective Establish Sewing Lines on segments of Patterns or Internal Shapes/Lines. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Segment Sewing 2D Toolbar ▶ Segment Sewing ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Segment Sewing 2D Toolbar ▶ Segment Sewing 2. Click once on the Pattern segment to establish the first half of the seam. 3. With the mouse cursor, hover over the segment to be sewn to the first half of the seam. Drag the mouse to make the the Directional Notches parallel to each other. Then, click to establish the second half of the seam. ※ Note * When Directional Notches are crossed, the Sewing Lines in the 3D window are crossed as well. When Patterns are simulated at this state, either one of the Patterns is reversed and then sewn to the other Pattern. * When establishing the second half of the seam, difference in the Sewing Line lengths appears in blue next to the mouse cursor. If the difference exceeds 1 inch, the difference appears in red to alert the user. * Use the shortcut to establish M:N Sewing Lines. For more detail, please reference M:N Segment Sewing.
content_description: Establish precise sewing lines on pattern segments using the Segment Sewing tool to ensure accurate seam alignment and prevent errors in 3D simulation.

title: Replace as Pattern Outline
content: ### Objective Substitute Pattern outlines with Internal Lines, establishing the Internal Line as the new Pattern outline. ### Location 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern ### Operation 1. Create an internal line to be substituted with the Pattern outline. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern 3. Click on the Internal Line and the Pattern outline that should be replaced. → The Internal Line and Pattern outline are highlighted in yellow. 4. Right-click on the selected Internal Line or Pattern outline. → A pop-up menu appears. 5. Select the Replace as Pattern Outline option. → The selected Pattern outline is replaced with the shape of the Internal Line. → The original Pattern outline appears as a Reference Line.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for substituting Pattern outlines with Internal Lines in a 2D design environment.

title: Edit AI Bezier Curve
content: ### Objective Edit AI Bezier curves with editing tools. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Curve Point or Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar▶ Edit Curve Point or Edit Pattern ### Operation #### Edit Curvature 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Curve Point or Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar▶ Edit Curve Point or Edit Pattern 2. Click the point on the AI Bezier Curve to access the handle. 3. When the handle appears, click and drag the point on the desired end of the handle to change the curvature. ※Note: * To edit only one side's curvature, hold down the Alt key on the keyboard while click and dragging the point on the desired end of the handle. * To maintain the handle's angle while changing the curvature, press down the Ctrl key on the keyboard then click and drag the curve. (ver MD10) #### Convert a Segment Point to an AI Bezier Curve 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Curve Point or Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar▶ Edit Curve Point or Edit Pattern 2. To convert a Segment Point to an AI Bezier curve, hold down the Alt key on the keyboard, and then click and drag the desired Segment Point. → The selected Segment Point is converted to an AI Bezier curve as the blue handle appears. #### Delete Handles 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Curve Point or Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar▶ Edit Curve Point or Edit Pattern 2. Click the Segment Point on the curve. → The pair of handles appear. 3. Right click on the point on the desired handle to access the pop-up menu. Then, select Delete Point. Or, hit the Delete key on the keyboard. → The selected handle is deleted and the curve is converted to a straight line. ※Note: To delete the pair of handles at once, hold down the Alt key on the keyboard and select the Segment Point on the curve.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for editing AI Bezier curves using various tools and keyboard shortcuts to customize curvature and convert segment points effectively.

title: Mode
content: ### Objective Marvelous Designer provides total of five Mode as follows: Simulation, Animation, Modular, UV Editor and Sculpt Mode. ### Location Switch between Mode using the button on the right-top corner of the window. ### Operation Simulation Mode is a mode where it is possible to create and edit patterns in the 2D Window or animate draping of Garments, Poses, or Actions in the 3D Window. Animation Mode is a mode where it is possible to record, play and edit Garment animations. Modular Mode is a mode where it is possible to mix and match Garment components, such as sleeves and collars, as blocks to test and create new styles. UV Editor Mode is a mode where editing UV of Garment. (Ver. MD 7.5) Sculpt Mode Sculpt garments using various brush tools. (ver. MD8)
content_description: Explore the five versatile modes of Marvelous Designer—Simulation, Animation, Modular, UV Editor, and Sculpt Mode—designed to enhance your garment creation and editing experience.

title: Internal Polygon/Line
content: ### Objective Create Internal Polygons and Lines inside a Pattern. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ Internal Polygon/Line 2D Toolbar ▶ Internal Polygon/Line ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ Internal Polygon/Line 2D Toolbar ▶ Internal Polygon/Line 2. Click within a Pattern to establish the start point of an Internal Polygon/Line. 3. Drag the mouse and click as needed to freehand the Internal Polygon/Line. 4. Right click while freehanding the Internal Polygon/Line to access the Create Internal Polygon/Line window. 5. Use Length, Mirror Creation, and Position options to create the Internal Polygon/Line more precisely and conveniently. Option | Description ---|--- Length | Length | Designate the length to be created next. When the Mirror Creation option is active, the Length will be applied to the mirrored line as well. Option (ver5.1.0) | Mirror Creating | The Internal Polygon/Line is created symmetrically. The starting point converts to a closed point. Axis | Local | Symmetric lines are created based on the starting point (local). X-Axis | Symmetric lines are created based on the X-Axis. Y-Axis | Symmetric lines are created based on the Y-Axis. Position | Left | Set the distance between the Internal Polygon/Line and the Pattern outline on its left. Right | Set the distance between the Internal Polygon/Line and the Pattern outline on its right. Top | Set the distance between the Internal Polygon/Line and the Pattern outline on its top. Bottom | Set the distance between the Internal Polygon/Line and the Pattern outline on its bottom. 6. To complete an Internal Polygon, click the start point. On the other hand, to complete an Internal Line, double click the last point. ※ Note: * Right click inside a Pattern to open the Create Internal Polygon window and type in desired values. → An Internal Polygon is created with the designated values (ver2.5.0). * Click inside a Pattern to create the start point of an Internal Line. Then, drag and right click to open the Create Internal Polygon window. Enter desired values. → An Internal Line is created with the designated values (ver2.5.0). * Hold down the Ctrl key as creating an Internal Polygon/Line to create curves. * Hold down the Shift key to drag the mouse in straight lines or in 45º diagonal lines. ※ Note: Internal Shape Tool Group ※ Note: Mirror Creating
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide on how to create internal polygons and lines within a 2D pattern using the designated tools and options for precise customization.

title: M:N Free Sewing (2D)
content: ### Objective Freely establish Sewing Lines on Pattern outlines and Internal Shapes/Lines to sew multiple Patterns (M) to multiple Patterns (N) at once. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ M:N Free Sewing 2D Toolbar ▶ M:N Free Sewing ※ Note: Hold down the Free Sewing tool for a while to access the M:N Free Sewing Tool. ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ M:N Free Sewing 2D Toolbar ▶ M:N Free Sewing 2. Establish Free Sewing Lines on multiple Patterns, which are considered as M Patterns. 3. Hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete. → The Sewing Lines appear in neon color. 4. While being mindful of Directional Notches, establish Sewing Lines on Patterns which are sewn to M Patterns. Hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete M:N Sewing Lines. → All Sewing Lines no longer appear in neon color. ※ Note: * While establishing the Sewing Lines, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action or hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel all actions. * While establishing M:N sewing lines, if you click on an inappropriate segment, the segment appears in red and the Sewing Line cannot be applied. * The difference in lengths between the first and second half seams appears in blue next to the mouse cursor. When the difference is greater than 1 inch, it turns red to alert the user.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for users to efficiently establish sewing lines between multiple patterns using the M:N Free Sewing tool.
